claim_decisions.statement: In the March–April 2022 returnee survey, nearly 75% of surveyed farming households reported lower harvests than in 2014; over 80% of livestock owners reported smaller herds.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Self-reported; multiple drivers discussed. Historical 2022 responses, not a 2026 assessment.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, reduced rainfall and water scarcity reported by participants in Nimrud and Hatra.
pathways.documented_impact: The qualitative assessment describes weakened farming livelihoods and agricultural productivity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competition for irrigation and land interacts with unequal access, exclusion and weak services.
pathways.possible_consequence: Participants describe farmer-herder tensions in Nimrud and resource/service pressures in Hatra; further stress could intensify existing grievances, not necessarily produce violence.
alternative_explanations: Post-conflict recovery, unemployment, patronage, service inequality and political influence also shape grievances independently of climate.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated qualitative mechanism from purposive February 2026 fieldwork; no causal estimate, representative prevalence or attribution to anthropogenic climate change.
resilience_factors: Tribal mediation, shared economic activity and community networks are described capacities, not evaluated effects; less-connected groups can be excluded.
pathways.compact_statement: In Nimrud/Hatra, participants link water stress and farming losses with irrigation/land competition and existing grievances; local peace capacities are unevenly accessible.

executive_assessment.text: New February 2026 fieldwork adds a local mechanism in Nimrud and Hatra: water stress and farming losses interact with irrigation/land competition and exclusion. These are participants' reported dynamics, not a representative causal estimate.

Evidence on return agriculture and displacement-site water access is dated 2022 and 2024. It documents economic and conflict-recovery barriers alongside climate stress, with local mediation capacities that can exclude less-connected groups.
